title: Cr.M (BA) No. 326-A of 2026 Noor Muhammad  Vs  The State, etc.
text:
1
Judgment Sheet
PESHAWAR HIGH COURT, ABBOTTABAD BENCH
(JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT)
Cr. M (BA) No.326-A/2026
Noor Muhammad.
…(Petitioner)
versus
The State, etc.
… (Respondents)
Present: Mr. Shad Muhammad Khan, Advocate for
petitioners.
Mr. Basharat Khan, Additional Advocate
General for State.
Date of hearing: 21.05.2026
ORDER
SYED MUDASSER AMEER, J.- This single order
disposes of the instant bail petition moved by petitioner
Noor Muhammad as well as connected Cr. M No.329-
A/2026 titled Mst. Asima Bibi, etc. v. The State, etc.,
moved by petitioners Mst. Asima Bibi wife of Shabbir and
Mst. Madiha Bibi wife of Faisal, as both petitions arise out
of FIR No.549 dated 02.05.2026 registered under sections
371-A and 371-B PPC at Police Station City, Mansehra.
2. Petitioner Noor Muhammad also filed Cr. M No.106-
A/2026 seeking correction of FIR number mentioned in the
__________________________________
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Syed Mudasser Ameer.
2
bail petition on the ground that due to inadvertence the FIR
number was typed as 540 instead of 549. The application is
allowed. Office shall make necessary correction.
3. Heard. Record perused.
4. As per contents of the FIR, on receipt of a public
complaint regarding alleged use of a rented house situated
at Tanki Mor, Mansehra for prostitution, the local police
conducted a raid whereupon petitioner Madiha Bibi along
with petitioner Noor Muhammad were allegedly found in
one room, whereas petitioner Asima Bibi along with one
Saifullah, who allegedly escaped from the spot, were found
in another room.
5. Significantly, there is no allegation in the FIR that the
present petitioners or any other person was engaged in
buying, selling, trafficking, hiring or commercial dealing
of any human being for purposes of prostitution. There is
also no allegation that any money was recovered, any
customer was found negotiating such transaction, or that
any material indicative of organized prostitution or
trafficking was secured during the raid.
6. Sections 371-A and 371-B PPC are intended to curb
trafficking, sale, purchase and commercial exploitation of
human beings for purposes of prostitution. Mere allegation
__________________________________
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Syed Mudasser Ameer.
3
of immoral conduct or mere presence of a male and female
inside a private premises does not ipso facto attract the said
provisions unless material exists showing buying, selling,
hiring, trafficking or commercial sexual exploitation of a
person. Reference in this regard may be made to Khalida
Bibi and another v. The State and others (2024 P Cr. LJ
1972), Bilal Jan v. The State (2021 P Cr. LJ 323), Mst.
Kainat v. The State (2016 YLR 974) and Shafqat Ali v. The
State (2009 YLR 60).
7. The contents of the FIR, even if accepted at their face
value, do not prima facie disclose the essential ingredients
of sections 371-A or 371-B PPC. At best, the allegations
merely suggest presence of opposite genders inside a
private house. Such circumstance by itself does not
constitute the offences alleged. In Khalida Bibi and
another v. The State and others (2024 P Cr. LJ 1972), it
was specifically held that even where a male and female
are found in an objectionable condition, sections 371-A
and 371-B PPC are not automatically attracted unless
material exists showing sale, purchase or hiring of a person
for prostitution.
8. The manner in which the raid was conducted also
raises serious legal and constitutional concerns.
Admittedly, the raid was carried out at a private dwelling
__________________________________
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Syed Mudasser Ameer.
4
house without obtaining any search warrant from a
Magistrate and without associating respectable persons of
the locality. Such intrusion into a private home,
particularly involving arrest of women, directly touches
upon the constitutional guarantees relating to dignity of
man, privacy of home and liberty protected under Articles
4, 9 and 14 of the Constitution. In Salman Ghazanfar v.
The State (2018 MLD 1446), this Court observed that raid
at a private premises without obtaining search warrant and
without compliance of section 103 Cr.P.C. amounted to
unlawful intrusion prohibited by law. Similar view was
expressed in Mst. Kainat v. The State (2016 YLR 974) and
Mohabat v. State (2019 YLRN 51 Karachi).
9. Courts have repeatedly cautioned that under the garb
of offences relating to prostitution and immorality,
constitutional protections available to citizens cannot be
permitted to be violated through arbitrary police action
founded merely upon suspicion, anonymous complaints or
spy information. In Mohabat v. State (2019 YLRN 51
Karachi), it was observed that no police official should be
allowed immunity for degrading dignity and reputation of
citizens through unlawful intrusion into private life.
10. Even otherwise, where allegations merely relate to
consensual intercourse or fornication, prosecution, if any,
__________________________________
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Syed Mudasser Ameer.
5
could only proceed through complaint under section 203-C
Cr.P.C. and not through registration of FIR under sections
371-A and 371-B PPC. Guidance in this regard may also
be sought from Khalida Bibi and another v. The State and
others (2024 P Cr. LJ 1972).
11. For what has been discussed above, the case of the
present petitioners, at the very least, falls within the ambit
of further inquiry under section 497(2), Cr.P.C. Reference
may also be made to Akhtar v. Khawas Khan and others
(2024 SCMR 476).
12. Accordingly, both these bail petitions are allowed.
The petitioners are admitted to post-arrest bail subject to
furnishing bail bonds in the sum of Rs.100,000/- each with
two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the
learned trial Court.
13. These are the reasons for the short orders of even
date.
ANNOUNCED.
21.05.2026
(Jamil)
J U D G E
__________________________________
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Syed Mudasser Ameer.
headnote:
Sections 371-A & 371-B, Pakistan Penal Code, 1860—Scope and ingredients—Mere presence of
male and female at private premises—Whether sufficient to constitute offences under sections
371-A & 371-B PPC—Held: Sections 371-A and 371-B PPC are intended to curb trafficking, sale,
purchase, hiring and commercial exploitation of human beings for purposes of prostitution; mere
allegation of immoral conduct or mere presence of opposite genders inside a private premises does not ipso facto attract the said provisions unless material exists showing buying, selling, trafficking, hiring or commercial sexual exploitation of a person—Contents of FIR, even if accepted
at face value, did not disclose essential ingredients of offences under sections 371-A & 371-B
PPC—Case held to be one of further inquiry within meaning of section 497(2), Cr.P.C. — Khalida
Bibi and another v. The State and others (2024 P Cr. LJ 1972), Bilal Jan v. The State (2021 P Cr. LJ
323), Mst. Kainat v. The State (2016 YLR 974) and Shafqat Ali v. The State (2009 YLR 60) relied
upon. (Paras 5, 6, 7 & 11) Constitution of Pakistan, 1973—Articles 4, 9 & 14—Sanctity of home and dignity of
citizens—Police raid on private dwelling house without warrant—Legality—Held: Raid conducted
at a private dwelling house without obtaining search warrant from Magistrate and without
associating respectable witnesses raised serious constitutional concerns touching sanctity of
home, dignity of man and liberty protected under Articles 4, 9 and 14 of the Constitution—Courts
must remain vigilant that under the garb of offences relating to prostitution and immorality,
constitutional protections available to citizens are not violated through arbitrary police action
founded merely upon suspicion or spy information—Salman Ghazanfar v. The State (2018 MLD
1446), Mst. Kainat v. The State (2016 YLR 974) and Mohabat v. State (2019 YLRN 51 Karachi)
followed. (Paras 8 & 9) Criminal Procedure Code, 1898—Section 497(2)—Further inquiry—Applicability—Held: Where
FIR lacked allegations showing buying, selling, trafficking, hiring or commercial exploitation for
prostitution and prosecution case merely rested upon alleged presence of opposite genders inside
a private house, case of accused persons fell within ambit of further inquiry under section 497(2),
Cr.P.C., entitling them to concession of bail. (Paras 7 & 11) Criminal Procedure Code, 1898—Section 203-C—Fornication/consensual intercourse—Mode of
prosecution—Held: Even where allegations merely relate to consensual intercourse or fornication,
prosecution, if any, could only proceed through complaint under section 203-C Cr.P.C. and not
through registration of FIR under sections 371-A and 371-B PPC. (Para 10)
